checkpoint.scope: On-disk settings only; game memory/closed-client state not asserted. No settings writes, profiling changes, or game input.

implementation: Width option uses actual scoped refresh. Native width/style changes occur only OOC after canaccesstable succeeds for every preallocated button and duration label. No native geometry/unit/visibility values are queried. Stored initializer heights supply sizes. Public SetAuraGroupLayout updates flow widths. Denied access preserves existing live dimensions, sets pendingWidth/needs-sync, and retries through existing refresh/combat paths. No new polling or pool.

sourceEvidence.restriction: DenyTaintedAccessWhenAurasAreSecret; public canaccesstable(table) returns bool; public SetAuraGroupLayout changes elementWidth without inspecting active auras. The source restriction is conditional, superseding the earlier blanket one-time-only assumption.

native.scenario: After one manual reload outside combat, user changed Aura width(X) and confirmed existing live icons resize and remain visible.
native.scope: Selected test client only; no independent build/window resample or other-client/taint/FPS certification.

preserved: Accepted preview/live frame styling, live duration-font scaling, black outline/shadow, optional below60second numbers, zero-gap3x2 sides, counts/filters/swipes, saved data and Flux bindings.

rejectedRegression.behavior: Intermediate external display-sibling sizing candidate caused no visible buffs/debuffs in the native user test despite desktop passes. It was rolled back to the working timer/grid checkpoint before this guarded implementation. User then confirmed original aura display returned.
rejectedRegression.diagnostic: native=true ready=true buffs=true normalGroup=true classGroup=true row=true bound=raid1 error=default
rejectedRegression.retained: Rejected source and desktop logs preserved externally; they are not native acceptance or performance evidence.
